question: How are most sexually transmitted reproductive tract infections mainly spread?

options.C: Sexual contact with an infected partner

explanation: These infections are acquired primarily through sexual intercourse or intimate sexual contact. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is catching lower reproductive tract infections early so important for midwives?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any subsequent laboratory testing
options.B: It immediately restores normal hormonal balance in the ovaries
options.C: It prevents the infection from spreading upward into the uterus and tubes
options.D: It guarantees complete immunity against future bacterial exposures

explanation: Prompt treatment stops pathogens from ascending into the upper reproductive organs where they cause severe damage. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h1)

question: What term describes passing an infection from a mother to her baby during pregnancy or childbirth?
explanation: Vertical transmission specifically refers to the passage of pathogens from mother to child during the perinatal period. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why are adolescent girls biologically more vulnerable to certain sexually transmitted infections than older women?

options.A: Their pelvic bones are shaped differently during puberty
options.B: Their immune systems completely ignore bacterial invaders
options.C: They produce lower amounts of protective vaginal flora
options.D: Their cervical cells are more exposed and immature

explanation: Ectocervical maturation changes over time, leaving younger females with vulnerable tissue prone to pathogen penetration. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which organism typically causes a frothy, yellow-green vaginal discharge with severe itching?
explanation: Trichomoniasis is a parasitic infection classically characterized by a frothy, yellow-green discharge and irritation. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h3)

question: What makes Chlamydia trachomatis particularly challenging to manage in routine clinic visits?

options.A: It frequently causes no noticeable symptoms at all
options.B: It resists all known classes of oral antibiotics
options.C: It only affects women who have given birth before
options.D: It changes the physical color of the cervix permanently

explanation: Chlamydia is notorious for being a silent infection, meaning many infected women remain unaware until complications arise. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is syndromic management mainly based on when laboratory tests are not available?
explanation: Syndromic management uses clinical algorithms matching visible signs and symptoms to provide immediate treatment during the visit. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why are routine screening checks done during the first antenatal visit?

options.A: To determine the precise date when labor contractions will start
options.B: To measure the baseline hormonal levels of the expectant mother
options.C: To confirm the exact gestational age of the developing fetus
options.D: To detect asymptomatic infections before they harm the pregnancy

explanation: Screening catches hidden infections early, preventing vertical transmission and adverse pregnancy outcomes. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h4)

question: What condition can a newborn get during vaginal delivery if the mother has an untreated gonococcal or chlamydial infection?
explanation: Babies passing through an infected birth canal often develop eye infections known as ophthalmia neonatorum. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h5)

question: A postpartum woman develops severe lower abdominal pain and foul-smelling lochia a few days after delivery. What prior condition could have contributed significantly to this?

options.A: An untreated lower reproductive tract infection
options.B: Consuming too much spicy food during pregnancy
options.C: Failing to walk around early enough after birth

explanation: Pathogens present in the reproductive tract can easily ascend into the uterine cavity after birth, leading to postpartum endometritis. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why is treating only the female patient not enough when managing sexually transmitted reproductive tract infections?

options.A: It causes immediate allergic reactions in the newborn baby
options.B: It leaves the sexual partner untreated, causing reinfection
options.C: It stops the ovaries from producing normal progesterone
options.D: It permanently ruins the effectiveness of future antibiotics

explanation: Without treating partners, the woman faces almost guaranteed reinfection once sexual activity resumes. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the main goal of partner notification slips given to patients in the clinic?

options.A: To prove to the midwife that the patient is married
options.B: To track the exact home address of every community member
options.C: To encourage exposed partners to seek testing and treatment
options.D: To serve as a legal permit for receiving free medication

explanation: Notification slips discreetly invite partners to the clinic so they can receive necessary evaluation and therapy. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is a core way to prevent sexually transmitted reproductive tract infections?

options.B: Consistent and correct barrier method use
options.D: Avoiding all physical exercise during pregnancy

explanation: Condoms provide a physical barrier that significantly reduces the transmission of pathogens during intercourse. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why must midwives keep a non-judgmental attitude during sexual health counseling sessions?

options.A: To encourage patients to share accurate information without fear of stigma
options.B: To ensure the hospital meets international accreditation standards
options.C: To guarantee that laboratory test results come out much faster
options.D: To prevent the midwife from feeling stressed during working hours

explanation: A welcoming, stigma-free environment builds trust, making patients more honest about their symptoms and sexual history. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h7)
